prompt: Compare allopatric and sympatric speciation. Which is more prevalent?
correct: Allopatric : geographic separation reduces gene flow before divergence. Sympatric : reproductive divergence occurs without a physical barrier. Your professor identifies allopatric speciation as the most prevalent mode.

close.text: Allopatric speciation occurs without a physical barrier, whereas sympatric speciation begins when a geographic barrier stops gene flow; sympatric speciation is considered the more common mode.
close.whyWrong: The geographic relationship is reversed. Allopatric speciation begins with geographic separation; sympatric speciation occurs without it, and allopatric is the more prevalent mode in this course.

close.text: Allopatric speciation begins with geographic separation and sympatric speciation occurs in the same geographic area, but sympatric speciation is the dominant mode because gene flow accelerates divergence.

medium.text: Allopatric speciation is divergence caused mainly by genetic drift, while sympatric speciation is divergence caused mainly by natural selection; geography is not the defining difference.

medium.text: Allopatric and sympatric speciation both require populations to be physically separated first; sympatric speciation describes what happens if those populations later come back into contact.

clear.text: Allopatric speciation is the evolution of many species from one ancestor, while sympatric speciation is the merger of two species into one.
clear.whyWrong: The first describes adaptive radiation and the second resembles fusion, not the two geographic modes of speciation.

clear.text: Allopatric speciation happens only in plants through polyploidy, whereas sympatric speciation happens only in animals through behavioral isolation.

prompt: How do BMP4 and Gremlin affect bird-foot pattern formation?
correct: BMP4 promotes apoptosis of interdigital cells; Gremlin inhibits BMP4 and allows those cells to survive. Their relative spatial expression helps determine whether tissue between digits is removed or retained.
correctWhy: This matches the course-supported answer for this study-guide question.

close.text: Gremlin promotes apoptosis between the developing digits, while BMP4 blocks that cell death; stronger Gremlin expression therefore produces less webbing.

close.text: BMP4 and Gremlin both promote survival of interdigital cells; webbing is lost only when both signals are absent.
close.whyWrong: BMP4 promotes programmed cell death between digits. Gremlin opposes BMP4, so the two signals do not have the same effect.

medium.text: BMP4 determines which body segment will become a limb, while Gremlin sets the anterior–posterior identity of that segment; webbing is a secondary effect of Hox patterning.
medium.whyWrong: That confuses BMP4/Gremlin with Hox-style regional identity. In this example, BMP4 and Gremlin directly regulate interdigital cell death and survival.

medium.text: The two genes mainly change the timing of overall foot growth: BMP4 speeds growth and Gremlin slows it, producing different adult foot proportions.
medium.whyWrong: The lecture example is about apoptosis of tissue between digits, not just a change in overall growth rate.

clear.text: BMP4 and Gremlin are reproductive-isolation genes: one changes mating calls and the other prevents gamete fusion.
clear.whyWrong: Those are prezygotic isolation mechanisms, not developmental patterning genes in the bird-foot example.

clear.text: BMP4 forms the vertebral column and Gremlin forms the dorsal hollow nerve cord during chordate development.
clear.whyWrong: Those are chordate body-plan features, not the BMP4/Gremlin mechanism discussed in evo-devo.
